co_rifle.blurb: Rifle is a steep limestone canyon running north to south along East Rifle Creek near the town of Rifle, Colorado. Almost everything is bolted sport climbing on pockets, tufas and edges, much of it steep or overhanging and demanding power endurance. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.14, with the bulk at 5.12 and 5.13, which makes it one of the country's strongest concentrations of hard sport routes. Moderates are fewer, with the Ice Cave Walls holding the largest selection from 5.8 to 5.11. The main season is mid-April to mid-November, with spring seeps, reliable summers on the many shaded walls, and cooler fall days. In winter some of the canyon turns to ice.

mi_marquette_and_central_up_bouldering.blurb: Boulders around Marquette, in Michigan's central Upper Peninsula, near the Lake Superior shore. Nearly all of it is bouldering, with problems from the very easiest up to about V12, and most falling between V-easy and V5. The rock varies across the region, spanning gneiss or granite, quartzite and basalt or diabase; Slugg's Bluff, for example, is quartzite. The 550 Bouldering area holds most of the problems, while Slugg's Bluff Bouldering and Little Presque Isle add more. Some boulders sit high with views over the surrounding hills and lake, others line the lakeshore, and Little Presque has deep water solo problems. Fall brings cool temperatures and better friction, at Palmer in particular.

ca_happy_boulders.blurb: The Happy Boulders sit on the Volcanic Tablelands about seven miles north of Bishop, in California's Eastern Sierra. All the climbing is bouldering on Bishop Tuff, a volcanic rock that looks brittle but is solid, with finger pockets, steep juggy overhangs, crimpy faces and low traverses, plus highballs along the rim. Landings are mostly flat and the boulders sit close together. Grades run from V0 up to V12, with most problems between V0 and V4, so there is plenty for newer climbers. West Rim, East Rim and Central Happiness hold the most problems. The sheltered canyon is warmer in cold months than the higher, windier Buttermilks.

co_eagle_vail_minturn_red_cliff.blurb: This varied area around Vail, along I-70 west of Denver, sits at high elevation. Sport climbing and bouldering lead, with a good amount of ice and mixed and a little trad. Sport grades run mostly 5.9 to 5.12. Lime Park is a remote limestone canyon with the most routes, while Wolcott Crags and Boulders are on sandstone, and The Aircraft Carrier near Minturn has problems from V0 to V9. Rigid Designator Amphitheatre is the biggest ice venue, and ice and mixed lines mostly run WI4 to WI5 and M5 to M9. Rock cragging is generally limited to April through October because of the elevation, with cool mountain air and variable weather.

ca_donner_summit.blurb: Donner Summit sits on the pass just west of Truckee, California, with crags and boulders between Donner Pass Road and I-80 above Donner Lake. The rock is fine-textured, high-quality granite, with chimneys, slabs, overhangs and splitter cracks. Trad accounts for more than half of the climbing and sport most of the rest, with a little top-roping and bouldering. Grades run mostly 5.8 to 5.12 and a handful reach 5.14. Black Wall is the historic big wall at about 400 feet, and Snowshed Wall, Boreal Area and Grouse Slab hold the most climbs. Summer is the prime season, spring and fall can be excellent, and snow covers the summit in winter, though a few crags such as the southwest face of Grouse Slab stay climbable. Snowshed gets crowds, but a little hiking brings solitude.

mt_gallatin_canyon.blurb: Gallatin Canyon lies about twenty minutes south of Bozeman along US 191 in southwest Montana. Two distinct kinds of climbing share it. Limestone buttresses are met first when driving south, with steep, mostly single-pitch sport routes from about 5.10 to stiff 5.13, and one south-facing wall that can be climbed through winter. A few miles farther south is a high-quality gneiss area, nearly all trad, with multi-pitch routes from 5.6 to sustained 5.12. Bouldering adds a good share too. The East Side and West Side hold most of the climbing, with Stormcastle and the Retirement Crags among the other sub-areas.
